data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject only when it is installed as a fail-first authority before the subject's output is accepted, and the 3-of-26 result is explained by shown-to-fail-first installation converting tests from descriptions of behavior into registry-enforced guards that silently filter mutations before compilation reaches the guarded modules.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the 3-of-26 result were produced by a uniform mutation-testing tool with no installation-order dependency, the shown-to-fail-first mechanism would not explain the distribution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If compile.py mutations were evaluated after all module guards were installed, the 1-of-9 rate should match the 4/4 to 6/7 rates, contradicting the distribution.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a mutation that survives a shown-to-fail-first guard still produces a test failure, the guard was not actually installed as fail-first for that mutation.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the ordinarily-guarded modules' guards are not actually exercised by the mutations (e.g., mutations outside guard scope), the 4/4 to 6/7 losses would be unexplained by this mechanism.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"When a test is shown to fail before the mutation is introduced, the test becomes part of the installation ritual: the mutation is only accepted if it does not re-trigger the shown failure. This converts the test from a description (a statement about expected behavior that could be restated or derived from the subject) into a constraint (a necessary condition for installation). The 1-of-9 compile.py loss occurs because compile.py mutations are evaluated before any guard registry is populated, so only the one mutation that happens to be filtered by an already-installed shown-to-fail-first check is lost. The 4/4 to 6/7 losses in ordinarily-guarded modules occur because those modules' guards were installed with shown-to-fail-first authority, making them constraints on mutation acceptance rather than descriptions of module behavior.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
